en.title: Lanterns Premieres: Hal Jordan and John Stewart's Decades-Spanning Mystery Unfolds
en.summary: HBO Max's new DC series, Lanterns, kicks off a sprawling narrative across thirty years, centering on the intertwined lives of Hal Jordan and John Stewart. The premiere expertly balances foundational backstory with a compelling mystery set to unfold across multiple timelines.
en.body:
The **Lanterns** series has officially landed on HBO Max, and it’s immediately clear this is no ordinary superhero procedural. From its opening moments, the show establishes a narrative scope that spans decades, weaving a complex mystery that connects the past, present, and future of two iconic Green Lanterns: **Hal Jordan** and **John Stewart**. The premiere episode takes us back to 1996, introducing a young John Stewart (played by Cairo Cash Lee) in a pivotal scene with his father, John Stewart Sr. (J. Alphonse Nicholson). This moment, where his father tests his courage by shooting an apple off his head, sets a powerful precedent for the character's journey, emphasizing a deep-seated need to overcome fear. This personal history is contrasted with the public revelation of **Hal Jordan** (Kyle Chandler) as the Green Lantern, a narrative that clearly resonates with the young Stewart.

The story then jumps forward to 2016, where a grown John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) is undergoing training to inherit the Green Lantern mantle from **Hal Jordan**. The dynamic between the two is immediately fraught with tension; **Hal** appears reluctant to pass on the responsibility, while John grapples with **Hal's** perceived lack of commitment to his tutelage. This strained mentorship forms the emotional core of the early narrative, hinting at deeper conflicts and unresolved issues between the two heroes.

## A Mystery Across Time

The central mystery of **Lanterns** is anchored in two distinct timelines: 2016 and 2026. In 2016, **Jordan** is investigating a murder in the seemingly quiet town of Rushville, Nebraska, suspecting an extraterrestrial origin. This investigation serves as the catalyst, linking back to events that will culminate a decade later. The series deliberately creates a void around the year 2006, leaving audiences to wonder about **Hal Jordan's** activities and the reasons behind his consciousness backup, a detail that promises to be a significant plot point. Executive producer **Damon Lindelof** has drawn comparisons to the structure of **True Detective's** first season, suggesting an emphasis on character-driven emotional mysteries rather than a straightforward whodunit.

## Fan Expectations and the Green Lantern Legacy

For fans of **Green Lantern** lore, **Lanterns** represents a significant live-action exploration of characters who have long been central to the DC Universe. The series’ commitment to a multi-decade narrative suggests a deep dive into the complexities of the Green Lantern Corps and the personal sacrifices involved in wielding such immense power. The initial setup, focusing on the mentorship dynamic and the lingering questions from the past, has already sparked considerable discussion online. Viewers are eager to see how the series will reconcile the vast history of **Hal Jordan** and **John Stewart** with the unfolding mystery, particularly the enigmatic events of 2006.

## What's Next

With the premiere episode setting a grand stage, audiences can anticipate **Lanterns** continuing its dual-timeline storytelling. The series is expected to gradually reveal the connections between the 1996, 2016, and 2026 storylines, unraveling the secrets behind the Rushville murder and the evolving relationship between **Hal Jordan** and **John Stewart**. Further details regarding specific plot developments and the full extent of the 30-year span are expected to be revealed in upcoming episodes.

Recap Image: John Johnson/HBO Max In 1996, John Stewart (Cairo Cash Lee) and his two brothers are watching TV at home late at night, a special covering the revelation of Hal Jordan’s identity as Green Lantern. Hal (Kyle Chandler), an Air Force test pilot, claims that he was given this assignment due to his lack of fear—that after losing a parent as a child, there is nothing that scares him. John’s brothers beg him to turn the television off as they’re clearly not meant to have it on when their father gets back. John Stewart Sr. (J. Alphonse Nicholson) arrives home in his marine uniform, and knows what the boys have been up to. He takes John Jr. into the backyard and makes him put an apple on his head, pulling out a gun. John asks his son what he’s afraid of. The boy says he fears nothing, and the apple is shot off his head. The two embrace and head back inside. It’s 2016, and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) is waiting to be picked up by Hal Jordan, who is meant to be teaching him to take over as the next Green Lantern. It is clear that Hal feels dubious about this task and the possibility of being replaced, while John is quietly frustrated that Hal isn’t teaching him much of anything. To make up for this, Hal gives John a test, taking off the ring and flinging himself from their moving car after telling John that there’s a good taco stand a few miles down the road. John manages to grab the ring as the car careens off a short cliff and crashes below. Walking on the road, he calls his father (Sherman Augustus) and complains that Jordan is trying to kill him. John Sr. asks if he truly wants this and reminds him that the job will be his if he wants it to be. John gets a message from the ring next, a holographic uploading of Hal that Lanterns are meant to update weekly—Hal’s upload is ten years old, and far more personable. He has a message for himself that John agrees to deliver. Image: John Johnson/HBO Max At the taco stand, Hal is signing autographs and taking pictures with fans; the daughter of one notes that her mother misses “the suit.” John arrives and delivers the message: There’s hail in Rushville, Nebraska. Hal immediately takes off, leaving John to find his own way there. On arrival, John finds a mass shooting crime scene at a football field, one that Hal hasn’t been permitted to join by the local sheriff, Kerry Kane (Kelly Macdonald).
